newsitem.title: USA: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-NEBRASKA ROUTS VIRGINIA TECH IN ORANGE BOWL.
newsitem.headline: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-NEBRASKA ROUTS VIRGINIA TECH IN ORANGE BOWL.

text.p: For the first time in four seasons, Nebraska was playing in a bowl game that would not determine the national championship. But the Cornhuskers played like the two-time defending champions they were.

Quarterback Scott Frost and Damon Benning ran for two touchdowns apiece and defensive lineman Jason Peter returned a fumble 31 yards for a score as sixth-ranked Nebraska overpowered number 10 Virginia Tech 41-21 Tuesday in the Orange Bowl.

The Cornhuskers (11-2) cost themselves any chance of an unprecedented third straight title with a loss to Texas in the Big 12 Conference championship game. But they bounced back with a superb all-around effort against the Hokies (10-2).
"As much film as we saw and as hard as we practiced down here, we were definitely ready to play football tonight," said Benning, who was named Most Valuable Player.
"We wanted to make amends for (the loss to Texas in) St. Louis," he added.
The Cornhuskers scored 17 straight points in each half and piled up 415 total yards as they won their third straight bowl game.

Benning had 95 yards on 15 carries, including scoring runs of 33 and six yards in the third quarter. Frost, who also completed 11-of-22 passes for 136 yards, had a five-yard TD run in the second quarter and a 22-yard scamper to seal the win with 3:26 to play.
The Cornhuskers played a nearly flawless game, committing no turnovers and just three penalties. They rushed for 279 yards and allowed Virginia Tech no return yards.

"Our idea tonight was to play physical football," Nebraska coach Tom Osborne said. "I was surprised that we moved the ball so well offensively because Virginia Tech's defence was stingy all year long."

Jim Druckenmiller was 16-of-33 for 214 yards and three TDs for the Hokies (10-2), who received a bowl alliance berth for the second straight year. But his second-quarter pitchout attempt was smothered and picked up by Peter, who rumbled into the end zone to give Nebraska a 17-7 lead with 3:36 left in the first half.
This year's game shifted from the ageing Orange Bowl to Pro Player Stadium. It was the first time the game was played in December.
There were three other bowl contests Tuesday.

In Shreveport, Louisiana, Dameyune Craig threw for two 372 yards and touchdowns and ran for another and Auburn escaped with a 32-29 Independence Bowl victory over 24th-ranked Army, which missed a 27-yard field goal with 33 seconds left.

Craig helped Auburn (8-4) build a 32-7 lead after three quarters but then saw Ronnie McAda engineered a fourth-quarter comeback for Army (10-2), which scored three TDs, then recovered an onside kick with 1:22 to go.

McAda found Bobby Williams for 27 yards to the Auburn 14 to set up a third-down field goal attempt by J. Parker, who had been 17-of-17 inside 40 yards. But the kick was wide right and Terry Bowden notched his first bowl win as Auburn coach.

"In a year where it seems like you've been snakebit, you just start to think bad things may happen," Bowden said. "But we just kept fighting and we came out on top. Army didn't deserve to lose, but we fought hard enough to win."

In El Paso, Texas, Stanford blanked Michigan State 38-0, in the most lopsided Sun Bowl in 18 years. The Cardinal (7-5) scored on an interception featuring a lateral, a reverse and a blocked punt as they closed the season with five straight wins.

Chad Hutchinson was 22-for-28 for 226 yards and a touchdown as Stanford compiled 495 yards while holding Michigan State to 227. It was the first shutout in the Sun Bowl since 1978, when Texas routed Maryland 42-0.
Stanford improved to 9-8-1 all-time in bowls and notched its first post-season shutout since 1936, when it blanked Southern Methodist in the Rose Bowl.
Michigan State (6-6) was shut out in a bowl for the first time since 1938, when it was beaten 6-0 by Auburn in the Orange Bowl.
In Atlanta, Jason DeCuir kicked an 18-yard field goal with 3:03 remaining and Howard scored 17 unanswered points to defeat Southern 27-24 in the Heritage Bowl.
